identity.title: MaxSup: Overcoming Representation Collapse in Label Smoothing

problem.claim: The paper addresses representation collapse and misclassification overconfidence induced by Label Smoothing (LS).

gap.claim: The precise cause of LS's overly tight feature clusters had remained unclear.

contributions.claim: Decomposes the LS-induced loss into correct-prediction regularization and misclassification error-amplification terms.
Proposes Max Suppression (MaxSup), applying uniform regularization by penalizing the top-1 logit rather than the ground-truth logit.
Reports that MaxSup restores intra-class variation, sharpens inter-class boundaries, and performs robustly across image classification and downstream tasks.

stated_novelty.claim: The authors distinguish MaxSup from LS through uniform treatment of correct and incorrect predictions and top-1-logit penalization.

author_reported_evidence.claim: The authors report that LS's error-amplification term reinforces incorrect predictions with undue certainty and exacerbates representation collapse.
The authors report feature-space analyses showing restored intra-class variation and sharper inter-class boundaries with MaxSup.
The authors report experiments on large-scale image classification and multiple downstream tasks confirming MaxSup as a more robust alternative to LS.

narrative_sequence.summary: LS is widely used for calibration and generalization, but is associated with misclassified-sample overconfidence and compacted representations.
The paper analytically attributes these problems to a correct-only regularization term and a misclassification error-amplification term.
MaxSup penalizes the top-1 logit to regularize correct and incorrect predictions uniformly.
Feature analyses and experiments report improved representation structure and robustness across classification and downstream tasks.

source_observation.claim: The abstract links a loss decomposition to a specific failure mode, then aligns the proposed modification with that diagnosed term.

lessons.interpretation: Separating objective components by prediction condition can make a mechanistic explanation and intervention directly traceable.
lessons.application: When introducing a training-objective change, decompose its terms under relevant error conditions and state which term the change targets.
lessons.exception: This framing is less suitable when the abstract lacks an analyzable objective or when performance claims depend mainly on factors outside the loss.

unknowns: No quantitative metrics, dataset names, baselines beyond Label Smoothing, or experimental conditions are provided.
The abstract does not specify the exact loss decomposition, the meaning of “more robust,” or whether all reported gains are statistically assessed.
The reported feature-space effects and task results are author claims and are not independently verified here.
